2607.05391.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
2607.05391.paper_summary: Scaling pre-training, post-training, and test-time compute have become the central paradigms for improving the capabilities of LLMs. In this work, we identify verification, the ability to determine the correctness of a solution, as a new scaling axis. To unlock this and demonstrate its effectiveness, we introduce LLM-as-a-Verifier, a general-purpose verification framework that provides fine-grained feedback for agentic tasks without requiring additional training. Unlike standard LM judges that prompt LLMs to produce discrete scores for candidate solutions, LLM-as-a-Verifier computes the expectation over the distribution of scoring token logits to generate continuous scores. This probabilistic formulation enables verification to scale along multiple dimensions: (1) score granularity, (2) repeated evaluation, and (3) criteria decomposition. In particular, we show that scaling the scoring granularity leads to better separation between positive and negative solutions, resulting in more calibrated comparisons. Moreover, scaling repeated evaluation and criteria decomposition consistently lead to additional gains in verification accuracy through variance and complexity reduction. We further introduce a cost-efficient ranking algorithm for selecting the best solution among candidates using the verifier's continuous scores. LLM-as-a-Verifier achieves state-of-the-art performance on Terminal-Bench V2 (86.5%), SWE-Bench Verified (78.2%), RoboRewardBench (87.4%), and MedAgentBench (73.3%). Beyond verification, the fine-grained signals from LLM-as-a-Verifier can also serve as a proxy for estimating task progress. We build an extension for Claude Code, enabling developers to monitor and improve their own agentic systems. Finally, we show that LLM-as-a-Verifier can provide dense feedback for RL, improving the sample efficiency of SAC and GRPO on robotics and mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
2607.05391.paper_summary_zh: 擴展預訓練、後訓練和測試時的計算已成為提升大型語言模型（LLMs）能力的核心範式。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們將驗證能力，即判斷解決方案正確性的能力，確定為一個新的擴展軸。<lb/>為了釋放這一潛力並展示其有效性，我們引入了LLM-as-a-Verifier，一個通用的驗證框架，能夠為自主任務提供細緻的反饋，而無需額外的訓練。<lb/>與標準的語言模型評估者不同，LLM-as-a-Verifier計算得分標記對數的分佈期望，以生成連續得分。<lb/>這種概率性表述使得驗證能在多個維度上擴展：(1) 得分粒度，(2) 重複評估，和(3) 標準分解。<lb/>特別是，我們顯示擴展得分粒度能夠更好地區分正面和負面解決方案，從而導致更精確的比較。<lb/>此外，擴展重複評估和標準分解始終能通過減少方差和複雜性來提高驗證準確性。<lb/>我們進一步引入了一種成本效益高的排名算法，用於根據驗證者的連續得分從候選中選擇最佳解決方案。<lb/>LLM-as-a-Verifier在Terminal-Bench V2（86.5%）、SWE-Bench Verified（78.2%）、RoboRewardBench（87.4%）和MedAgentBench（73.3%）上達到了最先進的性能。<lb/>除了驗證，LLM-as-a-Verifier提供的細緻信號也可以作為估計任務進展的代理。我們為Claude Code構建了一個擴展，使開發者能夠監控和改善他們自己的自主系統。<lb/>最後，我們展示了LLM-as-a-Verifier可以為強化學習提供密集反饋，提升SAC和GRPO在機器人技術和數學推理基準上的樣本效率。
